findings.description: The label version of IsPrimitiveCharacter calls IsPrimitive(q,n) instead of IsPrimitiveCharacter(q,n). No package intrinsic IsPrimitive(RngIntElt,RngIntElt) exists (verified by grep), so the call dispatches to Magma's builtin primitive-root test IsPrimitive(n,m), which requires n <= EulerPhi-ish bounds and raises a runtime error for essentially every valid label. The intrinsic is completely broken: every call with a valid Conrey label errors out. Correct behavior: return IsPrimitiveCharacter(q,n) (which is verified correct against Magma's IsPrimitive(chi) for all q<=40 and against LMFDB char_dirichlet.is_primitive for all 892 orbits with modulus<=100).

In the p=2, e>2 branch, the divisibility check misses the <-1> component: when n = -5^0 = 2^e-1 mod 2^e (s=-1, a=0, conductor 4) and v_2(qq) <= 1, the check IsDivisibleBy(a,2^(e-ee)) passes vacuously (a=0) and the intrinsic silently returns a wrong index (the trivial character, or even the invalid index 0 for qq=1) instead of raising the documented 'Target modulus must be divisible by conductor' error. The e=2 case one line above (line 916) handles this correctly via 'require ee ge e'. Composite moduli inherit the bug through the recursion (AssociatedCharacter(6,24,23)=5 silently drops the conductor-4 2-part; Conductor(24,23)=12 does not divide 6).

For N=2 the intrinsic returns 2, but the conductor of the (necessarily trivial) Dirichlet character of modulus 2 is 1; for N=1 it crashes with Min of an empty sequence. Cause: UnitGenerators(DirichletGroup(N)) is empty for N<=2, so V=[] and Set(V) eq {1} is false, falling through to 'if IsPrime(N) then return N' (N=2 -> 2) or to the Min over an empty list (N=1). There are no primitive characters of modulus 2, so 2 is never a conductor.

For a nontrivial character map with codomain Rationals() the intrinsic returns 2, but the docstring defines the result as 'the degree of the (cyclotomic) subfield of K generated by its image'; the image {1,-1} of a quadratic character generates Q, which has degree 1. This also contradicts the package's other Degree intrinsics (Degree(q,n)=EulerPhi(2)=1, Degree(chi)=1) and contradicts what this same intrinsic returns for the identical character embedded in a larger cyclotomic field (general branch computes Degree(sub<K|values>)=1). Only the codomain-Q special case is wrong.

The docstring promises 'note that only psi in the ambient group of chi will be returned', i.e. square roots that do not lie in Parent(chi) are silently omitted. But the code coerces every psi*xi into Parent(chi) via [Parent(chi)| ...], which raises a runtime error whenever a square root has larger order than the ambient group's base ring supports. E.g. the quadratic character in the default (rational) group DirichletGroup(5) has square roots only of order 4 (values in Q(i)); per the docstring the result should be [], but the call crashes. The math is otherwise correct: for chi in FullDirichletGroup(N), 3<=N<=24, SquareRoots agrees exactly with brute-force enumeration {psi : psi^2 = chi}.

ConreyConjugates(1,1) crashes because Integers(1)!1 is the zero element of the trivial ring and Order() refuses it. Correct result is [1] (the trivial character is alone in its orbit; label utilities elsewhere in the package accept modulus 1, e.g. ConreyLabel of the modulus-1 character is "1.1"). The crash propagates to ConreyIndexes("1.1") and ConreyLabels("1.1") (both call this via SplitCharacterLabel), while ConreyIndexes(chi) for the modulus-1 GrpDrchElt works fine and returns [1].

ConreyInverse(1,1) crashes even though the intrinsic's own require explicitly admits q=1, n=1 ('q ge 1 and n ge 1 and n le q and GCD(q,n) eq 1'). In Integers(1) the element is the ring zero and Magma refuses the negative power. Correct result is 1 (the trivial character 1.1 is its own inverse). Works for all q in [2..60].
findings.evidence:
> ConreyInverse(1,1);
In file "chars.m", line 961, column 39:
Runtime error in '^': Can not take negative power of non-unit
(sweep over q in [2..60], all n coprime: ConreyInverse returns ni with (n*ni) mod q eq 1 mod q — all pass)

findings.description: For N=1 or N=2 the unit-generator list is empty and LCM([]) raises 'Illegal null set/sequence'. The order of the (trivial) character of modulus <= 2 is 1. This also breaks IsReal(xi,N) for N<=2, which calls CharacterOrder(xi,N).

Signature typo: single colon instead of '::' makes the argument untyped (Magma parses 'GrpDrchElt' as an optional parameter name, not as the argument type). Consequently DirichletCharacter accepts and returns ANY value unchanged: DirichletCharacter(42) returns 42. This pollutes dispatch of a widely used constructor name; a mistyped call (e.g. passing an integer or a tuple) silently returns garbage instead of raising a signature error.
findings.proposed_fix:
Line 1143: replace
intrinsic DirichletCharacter (chi:GrpDrchElt) -> GrpDrchElt
with
intrinsic DirichletCharacter (chi::GrpDrchElt) -> GrpDrchElt

findings.description: Docstring says 'Value of chi_q(m,n) in specified complex field' but the arguments are (q,n,m) and the function computes chi_q(n,m) — the value of the character with label q.n at m (it calls ConreyCharacterAngle(q,n,m) and returns 0 when GCD(q,m)>1, in which case chi_q(m,.) is not even a character). Same swapped notation in ConreyCharacterRealValue at line 640 ('Real part of chi_q(m,n)'). All sibling intrinsics (ConreyCharacterAngle line 618, ConreyCharacterValue line 529) correctly say chi_q(n,m).
findings.evidence: Code inspection plus behavior: ConreyCharacterComplexValue(q,n,m,CC) = Exp(2*pi*i*ConreyCharacterAngle(q,n,m)) and returns 0 iff GCD(q,m)>1, verified numerically for q in {5,8,13,16,21}, all n, m in [-3..10]; i.e. it is chi_q(n,m), not chi_q(m,n).

findings.description: Stale docstring copied from an older 4-argument version: 'Given a modulus N, a positive integer n, a list of integers u giving standard generates for (Z/NZ)*, and a suitable list of integers v, returns the Dirichlet character ... mapping u[i] to zeta_n^v[i]'. The signature takes only (N, v); there are no arguments n or u, and v is a list of rational angles (n is derived as the LCM of their denominators), exactly as in the 3-argument version at line 1094.
findings.evidence: Signature is (N::RngIntElt, v::SeqEnum); body computes n := LCM([Denominator(e):e in v]) and maps UnitGenerators(N)[i] to F.1^(n*v[i]). Verified behaviorally: for N in [3..30] and all Conrey indexes n, DirichletCharacterFromAngles(N,ConreyCharacterAngles(N,n)) equals DirichletCharacterFromAngles(N,UnitGenerators(N),ConreyCharacterAngles(N,n)).
findings.proposed_fix:
Line 1107: replace the docstring with
{ Given a modulus N and a list of angles v returns the Dirichlet character with values in Q(zeta_n) mapping the standard generators of (Z/NZ)* (as returned by UnitGenerators(N)) to zeta_n^(n*v[i]), where n is the LCM of the denominators in v. }

findings.description: The string overload IsConreyConjugate(s,t) passes 4 arguments to the 3-argument intrinsic IsConreyConjugate(q,n1,n2), so it raises a runtime error whenever the two labels have the same modulus (the only interesting case; different moduli return false at line 363 before the bad call). SplitCharacterLabel returns [q,n], so the intended call is IsConreyConjugate(a[1],a[2],b[2]). The IsConjugate(s,t) intrinsic at line 367-370 delegates here and is broken the same way. Correct behavior: IsConreyConjugate("7.2","7.4") should return true (chi_7(2,.) and chi_7(4,.) both have order 3 and 4=2^2 with gcd(2,3)=1, so they are Galois conjugate).

findings.description: The OrderBound filter calls Order(q,n), which resolves to Magma's builtin Order(a,m) = multiplicative order of a modulo m, i.e. it computes the order of q mod n instead of the order of the character q.n. Since the trivial character n=1 is always in the rep list X, any nonzero OrderBound crashes with 'Argument 2 (1) should be >= 2' (order mod 1 undefined); even where defined the semantics would be wrong (order of q mod n, arguments swapped and meaning wrong). This makes the OrderBound option of ConreyCharacterOrbitRepIndexes and ConreyCharacterOrbitReps completely unusable. The intended function is CharacterOrder(q,n) (chars.m line 738); note the adjacent filters correctly use package intrinsics Parity(q,n), Degree(q,n), Conductor(q,n).
findings.evidence:
> Order(3,7);  // Magma builtin: order of 3 mod 7
6
> ConreyCharacterOrbitRepIndexes(13:OrderBound:=2);
Runtime error in 'Order': Argument 2 (1) should be >= 2
> ConreyCharacterOrbitReps(40:OrderBound:=2);
Runtime error in 'Order': Argument 2 (1) should be >= 2
(grep confirms no package intrinsic Order(q::RngIntElt,n::RngIntElt) exists; the character-order intrinsic is named CharacterOrder.)

findings.description: Both PrimitiveOnly sanity requires are wrong. Line 376: 'require ConductorBound eq 0 or ConductorBound gt 0' is vacuously true (should be ConductorBound ge q, since primitive characters mod q have conductor exactly q). Line 377: 'require ConductorDivides eq 0 or ConductorDivides mod q ne 0' is INVERTED: it rejects consistent requests (q | ConductorDivides) and accepts inconsistent ones (q does not divide ConductorDivides). Because the PrimitiveOnly branch returns early at line 392 without applying the ConductorBound/ConductorDivides filters, the accepted inconsistent requests silently return characters violating the requested filter.
findings.evidence:
> ConreyCharacterOrbitReps(5:PrimitiveOnly:=true,ConductorDivides:=10);  // consistent: 5 | 10
Runtime error in 'ConreyCharacterOrbitRepIndexes': Invalid ConductorDivides when PrimitiveOnly is set
> ConreyCharacterOrbitReps(5:PrimitiveOnly:=true,ConductorDivides:=3);  // inconsistent: 5 does not divide 3
[ 5.4, 5.2 ]   // returned characters have conductor 5, which does not divide 3
> ConreyCharacterOrbitReps(5:PrimitiveOnly:=true,ConductorBound:=3);    // inconsistent: conductor 5 > 3
[ 5.4, 5.2 ]

findings.description: IsCyclic(N::RngIntElt) claims to return whether (Z/NZ)* is cyclic, but the last disjunct IsPrimePower(N) accepts N = 2^e for e >= 3, where (Z/2^eZ)* = C2 x C2^(e-2) is NOT cyclic. Wrong answer (true) for N = 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, ... The only internal caller (chars.m:300, CharacterOrbitReps fast path) happens to be harmless because the Conrey path it wrongly selects is correct for all moduli (verified: CharacterOrbitReps(N) for N=8,16,32,64 matches the generic GaloisConjugacyRepresentatives path), but the intrinsic itself returns a mathematically wrong value to any user.

The q le 2 early return ignores PrimitiveOnly: ConreyCharacterOrbitReps(2:PrimitiveOnly:=true) returns ["2.1"], but the character 2.1 has conductor 1 and is not primitive; there is no primitive character of modulus 2 (LMFDB char_dirichlet modulus-2 row has is_primitive = false), so the result should be empty. (q=1 is fine: the trivial character mod 1 is primitive.)

IsMinimalSlow crashes on the trivial character of modulus 1 because Magma's IsPrimePower errors on argument 1 (and the non-prime-power fallback &and over the empty Factorization list would also fail). IsMinimal correctly returns true for modulus 1, so the two implementations disagree at N=1.
findings.proposed_fix:
Insert before line 92 (b,p,e := IsPrimePower(Modulus(chi));):
    if Modulus(chi) eq 1 then return true; end if;

findings.description: The Regexp patterns in IsCharacterLabel (line 142) and IsCharacterOrbitLabel (line 156) are unanchored, so any string CONTAINING a label substring validates: "x13.5y", "13.5.7", "13.c.7" are all accepted as valid labels, contradicting the docstring 'Determines if s is a valid conrey label q.n'. Everything downstream (DirichletCharacter(s), CharacterOrbitLabel(s), ...) silently accepts such malformed strings. Magma's Regexp supports ^/$ anchors (verified).

Docstring says 'The order of the characters in the specified character orbit' but the intrinsic returns the DEGREE EulerPhi(order) (= size of the orbit / degree of Q(chi)); copy-paste from CharacterOrbitOrder directly above.

Docstring is a copy-paste from IsCharacterLabel: 'Determines if s is a valid conrey label q.n with n an integer in [1..q] coprime to q', but the intrinsic actually validates character ORBIT labels of the form q.a with a a base-26 string, returning (true, q, orbit index).
findings.evidence: Source line 155 reads '{ Determines if s is a valid conrey label q.n with n an integer in [1..q] coprime to q. }' while the body matches Regexp("([1-9][0-9]*)\\.([a-z]+)",s) and returns Base26Decode(t[2])+1; e.g. IsCharacterOrbitLabel("13.c") returns true 13 3.
findings.proposed_fix:
Line 155: replace the docstring with
{ Determines if s is a valid character orbit label q.a with q a positive integer and a the base-26 encoding of the orbit index. }

findings.description: Silently returns a wrong conductor for imprimitive characters of composite modulus. The test for whether xi factors through modulus M compares xi(u) with xi(u+r*M) for all r, but u+r*M need not be coprime to N (only to M), in which case xi(u+r*M)=0 != xi(u) and the correct divisor M is wrongly rejected. Correct behavior: skip representatives u+r*M that are not coprime to N (chi factors through mod M iff chi(a)=chi(b) whenever a=b mod M and BOTH are coprime to N). Additionally, for N<=2 the function crashes (U is empty, so Set(V) eq {1} is false for the empty V, and Min of the empty M-list at line 875 errors) instead of returning 1; and 'return Min(...)' leaks a second return value (Min's position) though one value is declared. Oracle: Magma's built-in Conductor(chi) on the identical character.

For a nontrivial character with rational codomain (i.e. a quadratic character with values in Q), returns 2 instead of 1. The docstring says it returns the degree of the subfield of K generated by the image; the image {1,-1} generates Q, degree 1. Both sibling intrinsics Degree(q,n) and Degree(chi::GrpDrchElt) return EulerPhi(order)=1 for quadratic characters, and this intrinsic's own general branch (line 883) returns 1 for the same character embedded in a larger field, so the rational-codomain fast path contradicts the general path.

Returns 1 instead of 0 at entries m in S with gcd(m,q)>1. ConreyCharacterAngles uses angle 0 as the flag for 'value is 0' (the angle of the value 1 is normalized to 1, not 0), but this function exponentiates all angles unconditionally, so e(0)=1 is returned where the character value is 0. The scalar sibling ConreyCharacterComplexValue (line 636) correctly returns 0.

Calls IsPrimitive(q,n) instead of IsPrimitiveCharacter(q,n). IsPrimitive(q,n) is Magma's built-in primitive-root test (is q a primitive root mod n), which raises a runtime error for essentially every valid label (it requires argument 1 < n), so the label version of this intrinsic never works; even where it did not error it would compute the wrong predicate.

In the 2-adic branch with e>=3, the require that the target modulus be divisible by the conductor ignores the sign s of the Conrey logarithm n = s*5^a mod 2^e. For n = -1 mod 2^e (s=-1, a=0; conductor 4, e.g. 8.7 or 16.15) and a target modulus qq with v_2(qq) <= 1, the divisibility check 2^(e-ee) | a passes vacuously (a=0) and the function silently returns the index of the trivial 2-part instead of raising the documented error - the conductor-4 character chi_{-4} cannot be induced to a modulus not divisible by 4. The parallel e=2 branch (line 916) and the odd-p branch (line 912) correctly raise the require in the analogous situation.

Crashes with a coercion error when chi lies in a Dirichlet group whose base ring cannot contain the square roots, instead of returning only the square roots in the ambient group as the docstring promises ('note that only psi in the ambient group of chi will be returned'). E.g. for the quadratic character mod 5 in DirichletGroup(5) (values in Q), the square roots have order 4 and cannot be coerced into Parent(chi); the documented behavior is to return an empty list.

Single colon instead of double colon in the signature: '(chi:GrpDrchElt)' declares an UNTYPED argument (with GrpDrchElt parsed as an optional parameter name), not an argument of type GrpDrchElt. Consequently DirichletCharacter(x) matches ANY x and returns it unchanged, silently propagating garbage instead of raising a signature-match error. Correctly-typed calls (string label version at 1153, (q,n) at 1148, genuine GrpDrchElt) still dispatch fine since more specific signatures win, so impact is limited to erroneous inputs being silently accepted.

findings.description: Crashes for q=1: Integers(1)!1 is the zero element of the zero ring and Order() refuses it. ConreyConjugates(1,1) should return [1] (the trivial character is its own only conjugate; compare ConreyIndexes(DirichletCharacter(1,1)) = [1] via the Conjugates(chi) path). This also breaks the label versions ConreyConjugates("1.1"), ConreyIndexes("1.1") and ConreyLabels("1.1").

Crashes for q=1 (allowed by the require q ge 1): Integers(1)!1 is the zero element of the zero ring and cannot be inverted. ConreyInverse(1,1) should return 1 (the trivial character is self-inverse). The label version ConreyInverse("1.1") crashes the same way. For 2 <= q <= 30 and all n the result was verified to satisfy 1 <= inverse <= q and n*inverse = 1 mod q.

Crashes for N <= 2: UnitGenerators is empty so LCM is applied to an empty sequence. Should return 1 (the trivial character). IsReal(xi,N) at line 891 inherits the crash since it calls CharacterOrder(xi,N).

Stale docstring, apparently copied from an older signature: it says 'Given a modulus N, a positive integer n, a list of integers u giving standard generates for (Z/NZ)*, and a suitable list of integers v, returns the Dirichlet character ... mapping u[i] to zeta_n^v[i]', but the intrinsic takes only (N,v); there are no parameters n and u, v is a list of rational ANGLES on the standard generators UnitGenerators(N) (integer entries denote the value 1, not zeta_n^v[i]), and n is computed as the LCM of the denominators of v. Correct wording along the lines of the 3-argument version at line 1095: 'Given a modulus N and a list of angles v on the standard generators of (Z/NZ)* (as returned by UnitGenerators(N)), returns the Dirichlet character with values in Q(zeta_n) mapping the i-th standard generator to zeta_n^(n*v[i]), where n is the LCM of the denominators in v.'
findings.proposed_fix:
Replace the docstring on line 1107 with:
{ Given a modulus N and a list of angles v specifying values on standard generators for (Z/NZ)* (as returned by UnitGenerators(N)), returns the Dirichlet character with values in Q(zeta_n) mapping the ith generator to zeta_n^(n*v[i]), where n is the LCM of the denominators in v. }

findings.description: Docstring says 'Value of chi_q(m,n) in specified complex field' but the arguments are (q,n,m) and the code computes chi_q(n,m) (= chi_q(n) evaluated at m); the sibling ConreyCharacterRealValue at line 640 has the same reversed subscript, while ConreyCharacterComplexValues at line 690 states chi_q(n,m) correctly. By Conrey symmetry the two agree when gcd(m,q)=1, but chi_q(m,.) is not even a valid Conrey character when gcd(m,q)>1 (where these functions return 0), so the docstrings should read chi_q(n,m). Not empirically demonstrable as a wrong value (symmetric where defined), hence filed as a note.
findings.evidence: Reasoning: ConreyCharacterAngle(q,n,m) requires gcd(q,n)=1 and returns 0 for gcd(q,m)>1; docstring subscript order (m,n) contradicts this asymmetric treatment and the sibling doc at line 690. Symmetry chi_q(n,m)=chi_q(m,n) for gcd(nm,q)=1 verified empirically for q in {2,...,48} (see test fragment).

findings.description: The branch 'if N le 2 then return [Rationals()|1:n in U]; end if;' at line 1066 is unreachable: for N <= 2 the only possible generator lists are empty (or contain units = 1 mod N), which the require at line 1063 ('#u gt 0 and ... n mod N ne 1') rejects first, so the intended graceful N<=2 handling never runs. All in-package callers (DirichletCharacterFromAngles) guard N < 3 themselves, so there is no behavioral impact today. The docstring also refers to 'the integers in S' although the parameter is named U. If the N<=2 case is meant to be supported, the require should be relaxed or the N le 2 test moved before it.

Declaration typos with no behavioral impact (Magma does not enforce declared return types): IsEven (line 815) and IsOdd (line 820) declare '-> RngIntElt' but return BoolElt (they are documented and used as booleans); ConreyLabels (line 1191) declares '-> SeqEnum[MonSTgElt]' (typo MonSTgElt for MonStgElt). Worth fixing for accurate signature listings.
